question: Three similar breaker poles read 40, 48, and 70 µΩ. No manufacturer limit is published. Which reading does the 50-percent-of-the-lowest rule tell you to investigate?
choices: 40 µΩ, because it is the lowest
explanation: Threshold is 1.5 times the lowest value: 40 × 1.5 = 60 µΩ. 70 µΩ is over that screen. 48 µΩ is not. There is no universal 100 µΩ ceiling in the ATS wording.

question: Why does a DLRO use a Kelvin (four-wire) connection?
choices: So the test can be done at 10 kV
So lead resistance and most clip drop are left out of the voltage measurement
So the meter reads megohms instead of microhms
So all three phases can be tested at once
explanation: Current uses one pair of leads. Voltage is sensed on a second pair inside those points, so the leads are not part of the ohm reading. Two-wire ohms on a microhm joint mostly measures the leads.
reference: Engineering fundamentals (four-wire Kelvin measurement); ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.6.1.2.B.2

question: ATS 7.2.2.D.8 on liquid-filled transformer winding resistance says temperature-corrected values shall compare within:
choices: 2% of previous results or of the adjacent phases
explanation: The winding-resistance screen is two percent, after temperature correction, against a previous test or the adjacent phases. One-half percent is the turns-ratio rule. Fifty percent is the bolted-connection rule. Three percent shows up on leakage reactance, not here.

question: A 200-foot low-voltage busway has no manufacturer insulation-resistance value. ATS 7.4.D.2.a minimum, corrected to the 100-foot basis, is:
explanation: Minimum megohms = 100 / length in feet = 100/200 = 0.5 MΩ. A shorter run has a higher minimum. Do not apply a withstand until the reading is above that floor.
reference: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.4.D.2.a (minimum megohms = 100 / length in feet)

question: On a four-wire micro-ohmmeter the potential clips belong:
choices: Outside the current clips, on the leads
Inside the current clips, on the joint itself
On the same stud as the ground lead only
One on the joint and one on the test-set chassis
explanation: Current enters outside. Voltage is read between the inner clips, so the drop in the current leads is ignored. Reversing that order puts lead resistance back into the reading.
reference: AEMC 6240 user manual, per manufacturer instructions

question: A two-wire ohmmeter on a 50 µΩ bus joint typically:
choices: Matches a Kelvin reading within 1 µΩ
Reads high, because the leads are in the measurement
explanation: Lead resistance is milliohms. The joint is microhms. Four-wire is how the AEMC 6240 and every other serious low-resistance ohmmeter drop the leads out. Then you still compare with similar joints under the 50 percent rule if the manufacturer is silent.
reference: AEMC 6240 user manual, per manufacturer instructions; ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.4.D.1

question: A copper winding measures 0.500 Ω at 20 °C. Corrected to an 85 °C reference temperature, it is about:
explanation: R at the new temperature = R measured × (Ts + Tk) / (Tm + Tk), with Tk = 234.5 for copper (225 for aluminum). 0.500 × (85 + 234.5) / (20 + 234.5) = 0.500 × 319.5 / 254.5 ≈ 0.628 Ω. Inverting the ratio gives 0.398 Ω.

question: When measuring transformer winding resistance, the dc test current should not exceed what share of the winding's rated current?
explanation: More current than about 15% of rated heats the winding during the test, which changes the resistance you are trying to read. The liquid-immersed and dry-type test codes and the C57.152 field guide all use that ceiling. ATS-2025 7.2.2.B.8 is tighter for acceptance work: it caps the current at 10% and credits C57.152 for the figure, so follow ATS when you are testing to ATS.

question: You measure a delta winding terminal to terminal with the delta closed: 0.20 Ω, 0.20 Ω, and 0.20 Ω. The total winding resistance you report is:
explanation: With the delta closed, the total is the sum of the three readings times 1.5: 0.60 × 1.5 = 0.90 Ω. (Each closed-delta reading is one phase in parallel with the other two, which is two-thirds of one phase.) For a wye measured terminal to terminal, the sum is divided by 2. Source: IEEE C57.12.90-2021, 5.4.1 and 5.4.2.

question: Wye winding resistance on the same tap reads 1.000, 1.010, and 1.045 mΩ by phase. What do you make of it?
choices: The third phase is more than 2% from the others, so look for a loose connection, broken strands, or tap-changer contact trouble
All within 5%, so no comparison is needed
Resistance must be corrected to 75 °C before phases can be compared
A 4% spread is normal for any LTC
explanation: The guide expects phases to agree within 2% of each other. 1.045 is about 4.5% above 1.000. Because the comparison is phase to phase, temperature correction is not normally needed on site.

question: After a winding resistance test on a large power transformer, the leads should come off:
choices: Only after the test set shows the winding is fully discharged, because stored energy can produce a large inductive kick
Immediately, since dc leaves no stored energy
Once the current display reads zero, even if the discharge light is still on
explanation: The dc current stores energy in the winding's inductance. Breaking the circuit early can produce a dangerous voltage spike. Use a test set with a discharge circuit and an indicator, and wait for it to clear.
